correctness.rationale: In the precise reverse-complement-closed, no fixed strands, one-deletion length-four DNA model, there are 120 candidate pairs of complementary orbits. Each pair is internally deletion compatible. Valid codes correspond bijectively to cliques in their 120-vertex graph with adjacency exactly disjoint deletion shadows (64 possible observed 3-mers). A rigorously bounded clique search proves no 12-clique and counts 44 11-cliques (22 codewords), with exactly nine alphabet-symmetry orbits of sizes 4 seven times and 8 twice and only universal representatives AAAA and CCCC. An independently implemented Python Bron–Kerbosch search over the actual definitions visited 3,867,602 calls and confirmed 44 maxima, nine orbit classes, and compulsory Watson–Crick pairs; its completeness follows maximal-clique enumeration plus an already bounded maximum. This proves a finite exact statement and does not extrapolate to other block lengths.
